cohort: 783 women with singleton pregnancies in cephalic presentation, gestational age >36 weeks, and no contraindications for vaginal delivery
finding: The HC/MH ratio was independently associated with Cesarean section for labor dystocia and performed better than fetal head circumference or maternal height alone in predicting this outcome.
mod_finding: A higher fetal head-circumference-to-maternal-height ratio was associated with an increased likelihood of cesarean section for labor dystocia.
